To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) listeners can be accurate in recognizing and interpreting auditory icons that are “loaded” with multiple information parameters; 2) recognition rate is consistently high when the listener responds to one, two, or three of the parameters; 3) recognition rate is significantly poorer when the listener responds all four of the parameters; and 4) the type of icon, as well as the parameter manipulation, has a significant effect on recognition and interpretation accuracy.
the manipulation of acoustic parameters of auditory icons can be used to convey multiple parameters of information about the sound source.

1) listeners can be taught to recognize and interpret the direction, distance, and size of objects from auditory icons that are manipulated in pitch, volume ramp, and reverberant decay, 2) listeners can be trained to recognize auditory icons with high accuracy and 3) listeners can be successfully taught to interpret auditory icons with high levels of accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of environmental sounds in the context of a multimedia interface.
the development and application of auditory icons for conveying information about objects in a non-verbal manner.
the use of environmental sounds, or auditory icons, in the design and development of user interfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
auditory icons are a useful tool for communicating non-linguistic information, but that the number of parameters to be manipulated should be limited.
the auditory icons were not recognized as well when all four parameters were present, and that the dog bark icon and the direction parameter were most easily recognized and interpreted.
auditory icons can be used to convey information about size, distance, and direction, but that the information is not always recognized and interpreted accurately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
auditory icons have the potential to provide a rich and nuanced means to communicate information to human listeners.
the auditory icons we created were recognized and interpreted accurately and consistently, with the caveat that recognition rate was lower when the icon contained all four parameters.
the manipulation of parameters of auditory icons to convey information is feasible, and can be achieved with some degree of accuracy by human listeners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auditory system is capable of extracting information from auditory icons in a way similar to the way we process visual information.
auditory icons are a promising means to communicate nonverbal information in the context of a variety of applications, such as mobile devices, games, and other interactive systems.
the auditory icons we used were effective at communicating information about size, distance, and direction.
